judges.name: Alan O. Forst
judges.ballot_question: Shall Judge Alan O. Forst of the Fourth District Court of Appeal be retained in office?
judges.background: Alan O. Forst was appointed to the Fourth District Court of Appeal by Gov. Rick Scott on March 7, 2013 and took the oath of office in April 2013. He attended Georgetown University and earned his law degree from the Catholic University of America, according to The Ballot Brief. Before joining the court he spent more than two decades in federal positions in Washington, D.C. (including the Justice and Labor departments, the Merit Systems Protection Board and the EEOC), practiced at the Crary Buchanan firm in Stuart, and from 2001 chaired Florida's Unemployment Appeals Commission (now the Reemployment Assistance Appeals Commission) under Govs. Jeb Bush and Charlie Crist, according to his Federalist Society biography. He was previously retained by voters in 2014 (75.07 percent, per Florida Bar News) and in 2020 (percentage not located; the Florida Bar's 2020 lawyer poll showed 78 percent recommending retention). He lives in Martin County.

rulings.case: Restoration 1 of Port St. Lucie v. Ark Royal Insurance Co.
rulings.what_it_decided: The court held that a homeowner's insurance policy may require the written consent of all insureds and the mortgagee before a post-loss assignment of benefits to a contractor is valid. The decision disagreed with a 2017 Fifth District ruling on similar policy language; the Legislature later changed the assignment-of-benefits law in 2019.
rulings.note: Florida Politics reported the opinion was written by Judge Forst for a unanimous three-judge panel.

rulings.case: Peterson v. (Parkland shooting victims' families) - Scot Peterson civil appeal
rulings.what_it_decided: A three-judge panel (Judges Damoorgian, Levine and Forst) rejected former Broward school resource officer Scot Peterson's argument that a trial judge should have granted him summary judgment, allowing negligence lawsuits by victims' families to move toward trial. The court issued its ruling without a written explanation.
rulings.note: The Hill identified the panel members; no opinion author is listed because the decision was issued without reasoning.

rulings.case: Boca Raton cemetery sale attorney-fees dispute
rulings.what_it_decided: The panel ruled for the developer and law-firm defendants in a dispute over attorney fees arising from the $6.2 million sale of a Boca Raton cemetery. Judge Spencer Levine wrote the opinion; the Daily Business Review reported that Judge Forst joined it but 'seemed especially torn.'
rulings.note: Characterization of Forst's view is the Daily Business Review's.

judges.record_summary: Judge Forst's name appears on the Florida Bar's list of 22 district court of appeal judges who qualified for the November 2026 merit-retention ballot. He has twice been retained by voters (2014 and 2020). In 2013 Sunshine State News described him as a 'conservative jurist' when Gov. Scott appointed him, and the Federalist Society's website hosts a contributor biography for him; this guide does not characterize his judicial philosophy. Most of his publicly indexed recent decisions are unsigned per curiam affirmances; the signed opinion most widely covered in the press is the 2018 assignment-of-benefits insurance ruling. No organized campaign for or against his retention, and no 2026 Florida Bar merit-retention poll result, was found in the sources searched.

judges.name: Mark W. Klingensmith
judges.ballot_question: Shall Judge Mark W. Klingensmith of the Fourth District Court of Appeal be retained in office?
judges.background: Mark W. Klingensmith was appointed to the Fourth District Court of Appeal by Gov. Rick Scott and assumed office on June 27, 2013, after serving as a circuit judge in the 19th Judicial Circuit (2011-2013). He earned his bachelor's (1982) and law (1985) degrees from the University of Florida and an LL.M. in judicial studies from Duke University in 2016. Before taking the bench he spent about 25 years in civil litigation private practice, became board certified in civil trial law in 2001, and served as an elected commissioner, vice mayor and mayor of the Town of Sewall's Point. He served as the Fourth DCA's chief judge beginning June 10, 2022 (re-elected in 2023) and in January 2024 was elected president of the Florida Conference of District Court of Appeal Judges. Voters retained him in 2014 (74.27 percent, per Florida Bar News) and in 2020 (63.0 percent, per Ballotpedia).

rulings.case: Cole v. Universal Property & Casualty Insurance Co. (4D22-1054)
rulings.what_it_decided: The court held that Florida's 2021 requirement that homeowners give insurers pre-suit notice before filing a lawsuit (section 627.70152) is procedural and therefore applies to policies issued before the law took effect, affirming dismissal of a homeowner's suit. Other district courts later split on the question.
rulings.note: The Daily Business Review's coverage names Judges Klingensmith, Levine and Damoorgian as the panel; the search results did not confirm which judge authored the opinion.

sources.title: Court finds Florida law requiring pre-suit notice in insurance cases applies retroactively (Daily Business Review)

judges.name: Johnathan D. Lott
judges.ballot_question: Shall Judge Johnathan D. Lott of the Fourth District Court of Appeal be retained in office?
judges.background: Johnathan D. Lott (his first name is also spelled 'Jonathan' in some official sources) was appointed to the Fourth District Court of Appeal by Gov. Ron DeSantis in the fall of 2025; the governor's appointment letter was dated Oct. 30, 2025, and Ballotpedia lists him as assuming office on Nov. 12, 2025. He filled the vacancy created when Judge Ed Artau left the court for the federal bench. He earned his bachelor's degree from the University of Florida and his law degree from the University of Chicago Law School (2014), and previously served as an Assistant United States Attorney for the Southern District of Florida. DeSantis first appointed him to the 17th Judicial Circuit (Broward County) bench in November 2024, where he took office Jan. 1, 2025 and served in the family division. This is his first merit-retention election.

rulings.what_it_decided: A panel of Judges Gross, Ciklin and Lott affirmed a Broward circuit court ruling without a written opinion.

judges.name: Shannon K. Shaw
judges.ballot_question: Shall Judge Shannon K. Shaw of the Fourth District Court of Appeal be retained in office?
judges.background: Shannon K. Shaw, of Jupiter, was appointed to the Fourth District Court of Appeal by Gov. Ron DeSantis on July 17, 2025, filling the vacancy created by the resignation of Judge Martha Warner; Ballotpedia lists her as assuming office on Oct. 1, 2025. She earned her bachelor's degree from Duke University and her law degree from Vanderbilt University Law School. Before her appointment she served as an Assistant United States Attorney for the Southern District of Florida beginning in 2017, was an associate at the law firm Hunton & Williams, and clerked for U.S. District Judges K. Michael Moore and James King in the Southern District of Florida. This is her first merit-retention election.

rulings.what_it_decided: A panel of Chief Judge Kuntz and Judges Ciklin and Shaw affirmed the trial court without a written opinion.
